Coherent FM-CW radar systems were developed at 35 GHz and 94 GHz for radar cross section measurements.
The systems operate over incidence angles from 0 to 60 degrees.
Both systems can operate in FM-CW mode or be converted to pulse or pulse-compression modes with added hardware.
The 94 GHz system additionally functions as a total power radiometer for brightness temperature measurements.
Phase-locked loops are used to linearize the frequency sweep in FM-CW operation.
Quadrature mixers provide I and Q channels for phase-coherent detection.
The 35 GHz system uses a 12-inch parabolic reflector antenna; the 94 GHz system uses a 12-inch Cassegrain antenna.
Radar cross section is calculated by comparing detected power to that from a standard radar target with known RCS.
Radiometric calibration uses black bodies at known temperatures for absolute calibration.
The systems use a swept microwave frequency signal upconverted to millimeter-wave frequencies.
Directional couplers provide reference signals for power-level calibration of transmitted signals.
The 94 GHz system uses a variable attenuator as an ON/OFF switch for radiometer operation.
Received signals are downconverted to microwave frequencies, filtered, amplified, and mixed to baseband.
Hardware is housed in lightweight, weatherproof aluminum boxes with antennas protruding from one side.
Data acquisition computers sample and digitally process received signals, including FFT for range profiling.
Calibration signals are delayed to appear at distinct frequencies to separate them from target signals.
The systems are designed for field experiments measuring scattering coefficients from sea ice, vegetation, and oceans.
Full polarimetric capabilities can be implemented by adding polarization switches.
The 94 GHz radiometer measures noise power over 94.5 to 95.5 GHz band, downconverted to 2.5 to 3.5 GHz IF.
Integration time controls radiometric resolution by filtering noise components.
